stories.headline: Cyclone clouds tomorrow’s MPTC, ZPTC poll selections
stories.title: Cyclone clouds tomorrow’s MPTC, ZPTC poll selections
stories.summary: The situation poses practical challenges for moving polling staff and transporting election material and ballot papers to polling stations, particularly in villages where access routes have been disrupted.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The situation poses practical challenges for moving polling staff and transporting election material and ballot papers to polling stations, particularly in villages where access routes have been disrupted.
Amaravati: The November 5 polling for the MPTC and ZPTC elections is facing uncertainty as Cyclone Murasu continues to disrupt normal life across several districts of Andhra Pradesh.

With heavy rain, flooded streams and damaged road connectivity affecting rural areas, the State Election Commission (SEC) is assessing whether polling can be conducted as scheduled or needs to be postponed.
The impact of the cyclone has been severe across the undivided Krishna, Guntur, Prakasam and Nellore districts, parts of the Tirupati region and even areas of East Godavari.
Rural areas have been particularly affected, with rainfall continuing in several places and villages facing difficulties due to overflowing streams and rivulets.
In some locations, road connectivity has been completely cut off.
Even if the rain subsides by Tuesday night, restoring normal conditions by Wednesday morning could prove difficult.
District administrations are likely to remain occupied with assessing damage, undertaking emergency field operations and restoring essential services.
The availability of personnel for election duties has also emerged as a major concern.
Collectors in the affected districts are already grappling with relief and restoration work.
The SEC is in consultation with collectors to obtain a clear picture of the situation, including the condition of roads, accessibility of polling stations and availability of staff.
The Commission is examining whether normalcy can be restored in time for Thursday’s polling or whether the elections should be deferred.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc on beach road
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc on beach road
stories.summary: The protective walls and large boulders laid along the shoreline to check erosion have been displaced and scattered by the force of the waves
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Kakinada: The Uppada-Kakinada beach road has suffered extensive damage due to Cyclone Arnab, which struck the region in the last week of October, coupled with severe sea erosion along the coastline.
Drone photographs have brought to light the extent of destruction, particularly on the stretch between Nemam and Pallipeta crossroad.
The road, which was in good condition before the cyclone, has now been badly damaged, with several portions washed away by powerful sea waves.
The aerial photographs present a grim picture of the battered road and the damage caused to the coastal protection structures.
The impact of the cyclone has also affected the government’s efforts to protect fishing communities whose lives and livelihoods have been threatened by continuous coastal erosion.
The protective walls and large boulders laid along the shoreline to check erosion have been displaced and scattered by the force of the waves.

According to experts, the presence of Hope Island near Kakinada Port influences wave patterns along the coast, exposing the Uppada shoreline to severe wave action during cyclones and resulting in recurring erosion.
The coastal stretches near Konapapapeta, Pallipeta and Subbampeta were among the worst affected.
More than 30 houses along the coastline collapsed, while several electric poles were uprooted.
With the beach road badly damaged and connectivity disrupted, vehicular movement between Uppada and Kakinada was suspended.
Officials shifted residents from vulnerable coastal areas to safer locations.

The extensive damage to the Uppada road needs to be assessed not merely in terms of reconstruction costs but also in terms of its wider impact on tourism, transportation and the livelihoods of fishing communities.

stories.headline: Cyclone disrupts train services
stories.title: Cyclone disrupts train services
stories.summary: In a press release issued here on Tuesday, the Vijayawada Division of South Coast Railway regulated a total of 29 trains, including 19 in the UP direction and 10 in the DOWN direction, as a precautionary measure to ensure passenger safety.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In a press release issued here on Tuesday, the Vijayawada Division of South Coast Railway regulated a total of 29 trains, including 19 in the UP direction and 10 in the DOWN direction, as a precautionary measure to ensure passenger safety.

Vijayawada: Train services on the Vijayawada–Ongole–Gudur section were temporarily suspended after gale-force winds were recorded at Karavadi Railway Station amid Cyclone Murasu, disrupting rail operations in the region.
Apart from the temporary suspension of train movement on the Vijayawada–Gudur section, several trains were cancelled or rescheduled due to the adverse weather conditions.
Among the cancelled services were trains from Gudur to Secunderabad and Chennai Central to Vijayawada.

Several other trains were rescheduled, including services from Tirupati to Secunderabad, Chennai Central to Jodhpur, Chennai Central to Jaipur, Tambaram to Hyderabad Deccan and Kakinada Town to Tirupati.
Railway authorities said train services were being regulated at originating and en-route stations until further notice, depending on weather conditions.
The situation was being monitored, and further operational changes would be made as required.

Passengers have been advised to check the latest train running status through the National Train Enquiry System (NTES) app and official railway communication channels before commencing their journeys.
They have also been urged to confirm the status of their respective trains to avoid inconvenience.

stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu impact: 2 killed, crops damaged across Andhra Pradesh
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu impact: 2 killed, crops damaged across Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: Cyclone Murasu impact: 2 killed, crops damaged across Andhra Pradesh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu struck Andhra Pradesh, killing two and causing widespread damage.
The second cyclone within a week triggered extensive rescue and restoration operations.

At least two people were killed after severe cyclonic storm Murasu struck Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday, damaging crops, homes and power infrastructure across the state, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
The second cyclone to hit the state within a week made landfall early on Tuesday, submerging standing crops in 15 districts.
Krishna, Bapatla and Nandyala were among the worst-affected districts.
Heavy to extremely heavy rain was recorded in several areas before landfall.
Thousands of trees were uprooted and 2,750 electricity poles were damaged.
Officials said strong winds and heavy rain also damaged transmission lines, substations and key power distribution equipment, with Prakasam and Bapatla districts reporting extensive damage.

Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority Managing Director Prakhar Jain told Press Trust of India that at least two people had died in cyclone-related incidents and 12,230 people remained in cyclone shelters.
According to preliminary estimates, the cyclone caused losses of at least Rs 344 crore and affected crops across 52,459 hectares, Jain said.
As many as 312 houses were affected.
The government was also monitoring 814 minor irrigation tanks, of which 776 had been placed on alert.

stories.headline: Assam to seek CBI probe to find flood cause; sack government employee if involved in polygamy: CM Himanta
stories.title: Assam to seek CBI probe to find flood cause; sack government employee if involved in polygamy: CM Himanta
stories.summary: The Assam government has decided to terminate an employee, irrespective of religion, if he is found to be involved in polygamy, Himanta Biswa Sarma said
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Assam government on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) decided to write to the Centre for a CBI investigation to find the exact cause of the devastating floods in Sivasagar and Charaideo districts earlier this year, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said.
The government has also decided to terminate an employee, irrespective of religion, if he is found to be involved in polygamy, he added.

Addressing a press conference after a cabinet meeting here, Mr. Sarma said, "The State cabinet has decided to request a CBI probe to find the exact reason behind the floods in Sivasagar and Charaideo districts."
The government will send a letter to the Centre within the next 10 days, but the final call to hand over the probe will depend on them, he added.
"We want the exact cause to come out," he said.
The Dikhow River ravaged Charaideo, Sivasagar and Jorhat districts in eastern Assam a few months ago.
At least 108 people died in the floods in Assam this year, with huge damage to houses, schools, roads, embankments, cattle sheds, fisheries and health centres reported in the affected districts.
The CM further said the State Cabinet has approved amending the Assam Service and Discipline Rule, and inserted a new clause in relation to polygamy.
"The government servant indulged in polygamy will be dismissed from the service.
That will be a disqualification for future employment also," he added.
The cabinet has inserted Clause 6 of Rule 7 to include the stringent punishment, Mr. Sarma said.
"As UCC (Uniform Civil Code) has been implemented in Assam, it will be applicable for Hindu, Muslim, Christian, everyone," he added.

stories.headline: Karnataka High Court initiates contempt proceedings over ruckus created by lawyers’ group inside Chief Justice’s court hall
stories.title: Karnataka High Court initiates contempt proceedings over ruckus created by lawyers’ group inside Chief Justice’s court hall
stories.summary: The High Court of Karnataka on Tuesday began suo motu contempt proceedings against unidentified individuals amongst a group of advocates, who barged into the Chief Justice’s court hall and disrupted proceedings by creating ruckus
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: The High Court of Karnataka on Tuesday began suo motu contempt proceedings against unidentified individuals amongst a group of advocates, who barged into the Chief Justice’s court hall and disrupted proceedings by creating ruckus.

The group compelled lawyers present in the court hall to leave, objecting to their participation in the court proceedings despite a call to boycott court proceedings across the State given by bar associations, including Advocates’ Association, Bengaluru (AAB) to protest against the recent incidents of murders, attempt to murder of advocates in various parts of the State.

A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and Justice K.S. Hemalekha, which was conducting proceedings in the court hall, took serious exception to the conduct of the group of advocates and ordered registration of a contempt of court proceedings in this regard.
The Bench also ordered issue of notice to the AAB.
“Prima facie, we are of the view that this conduct amounts to contemptuous behaviour,” the Bench observed in its order.

The Bench expressed displeasure over the incident, particularly since it had earlier promised the association that no adverse orders would be passed against advocates, who abstained from court proceedings on account of the boycott call.

After initiation of contempt of court proceedings, a group of advocates led by AAB Treasurer Shwetha Ravishankar appeared before the Bench and tried to explain the situation and offered apology for the incident.
However, the Bench told her, “This is the High Court of the State, and if you think that anyone can barge in and start creating a ruckus, then the consequences must follow.”
The Bench told her that response of the association would be heard when the contempt petition would be taken up for hearing on November 19.

Earlier, a group of advocates led by AAB president Vivek Subba Reddy entered the court hall-2 and asked the advocates, including a senior advocate attending the court proceedings, to go out of the court hall.

However, a Division Bench comprising Justice Anu Sivaraman and Justice K.S. Bharath Kumar, which was conducting proceedings, took serious exception to the conduct of the office-bearers of the association.
Meanwhile, advocates attending the proceedings vacated the court hall-2 avoiding any confrontation.

stories.headline: Karnataka’s drought assistance proposal to Union government sees upward revision by ₹1,818 crore following changes in SDRF norms
stories.title: Karnataka’s drought assistance proposal to Union government sees upward revision by ₹1,818 crore following changes in SDRF norms
stories.summary: The drought relief has been revised from ₹20,585 crore to ₹22,400 crore
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Revising the proposal for drought relief from ₹20,585.73 crore to ₹22,400.58 crore, the State government has sought urgent intervention of the Centre for early consideration and release of drought assistance to Karnataka- currently facing one of the worst droughts in several decades.
The drought relief has been changed following the revision of assistance norms under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) by the Ministry of Home Affairs on October 26, 2026.

Seeking appointment of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara in letters to the three leaders, said that 226 taluks have been affected by drought and crops over 57.93 lakh hectares have suffered extensive damage causing an estimated loss of about ₹62,481.88 crore.
“The crisis has placed immense financial distress upon lakhs of farming families,” the letter said.

After the MHA changed the norms of SDRF for a period between 2026-2027 and 2030-2031, the Karnataka’s requirement towards crop loss input subsidy has gone up from ₹6,128.70 crore to ₹7,943.554 crore — an increase by ₹1,814.85 crore resulting in an overall increase of the State’s requirement from ₹20,585.73 crore to ₹22,400.58 crore.
The other components previously submitted have remained unchanged.

While Mr. Parameshwara welcomed the Union government’s decision that has helped revise the input subsidy cost, he said that even after revision it is still low at ₹11,000 per hectare for rainfed crops, ₹22,000 for irrigated crops, and ₹30,000 for perennial crops, as against the actual cost incurred on seeds, fertilizer, agricultural labour, irrigation and other essential inputs.

Questioning the Centre’s reliance on the 2015-2016 agriculture census data to determine eligibility for disaster relief, he said that the decade- old landholding data does not adequately reflect present agricultural realities and could potentially deprive eligible small and marginal farmers of assistance.
Instead, he urged the Centre, to consider adopting Karnataka’s FRUITS database, which provides a contemporary and verified basis for identifying beneficiaries.

Seeking appointment of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Deputy Chief Minister and Revenue Minister G. Parameshwara in letters to the three leaders, said that 226 taluks have been affected by drought and crops over 57.93 lakh hectares have suffered extensive damage causing an estimated loss of about ₹62,481.88 crore.

Revising the proposal for drought relief from ₹20,585.73 crore to ₹22,400.58 crore, the State government has sought urgent intervention of the Centre for early consideration and release of drought assistance to Karnataka- currently facing one of the worst droughts in several decades.

After the MHA changed the norms of SDRF for a period between 2026-2027 and 2030-2031, the Karnataka’s requirement towards crop loss input subsidy has gone up from ₹6,128.70 crore to ₹7,943.554 crore — an increase by ₹1,814.85 crore resulting in an overall increase of the State’s requirement from ₹20,585.73 crore to ₹22,400.58 crore.
